Digital PR service is a strategy used to increase a brand’s online presence through digital platforms, including social media, blogs, and other online media outlets. It focuses on creating and promoting content, engaging with target audiences, and building relationships with online journalists, influencers, and bloggers to earn high-quality backlinks, improve search engine optimization (SEO), and enhance overall online reputation. Digital PR services aim to maximize a brand’s visibility and credibility online, driving more traffic to their website and boosting their market position. What are digital PR examples? Digital PR examples include creating and promoting online press releases, engaging in social media campaigns that aim to increase brand visibility and improve reputation, and collaborating with influencers or bloggers for product reviews, endorsements, or content creation. It also encompasses strategies such as search engine optimization (SEO) to enhance online articles and media mentions, or organizing virtual events and webinars that attract media attention and engage the target audience. These examples leverage digital platforms to boost a company’s presence and credibility on the internet. How much does digital PR cost? The cost of digital PR can vary widely depending on several factors such as the scope of the campaign, the reputation and size of the agency, and the specific goals of the client. Typically, small to mid-size businesses might expect to spend anywhere from $2,000 to $10,000 per month on digital PR services. Larger companies or more extensive campaigns can see costs exceeding $20,000 per month, especially when incorporating high-end content creation, influencer partnerships, and multimedia assets. What is the difference between PR and digital PR? The difference between PR (Public Relations) and digital PR primarily revolves around the platforms and strategies they employ to achieve their goals. Traditional PR focuses on building relationships and managing a company’s reputation through mainstream media channels like newspapers, television, and radio. In contrast, digital PR leverages online platforms such as social media, blogs, websites, and other digital channels to reach and engage with a wider, internet-savvy audience, aiming to increase online presence, improve search engine rankings, and foster direct two-way communication with consumers. What is SEO and PR? PR earns attention and coverage; SEO converts that authority into search visibility. Run together, a single piece of research can produce coverage, links and rankings at once. How much should digital PR cost? Campaigns commonly run $3,000 to $15,000 per month depending on how much original research is involved. How does Digital PR differ from traditional PR? Digital PR shares the same goal as traditional PR but differs in its approach, channels, and strategies. Digital PR focuses more on building brand awareness and authority than promoting products and services. Additionally, digital PR can reach a more targeted audience, be tracked through analytics, and be faster and more flexible than traditional PR. How much does Digital PR cost? Identify Your Specific Needs and Goals There are many exceptional digital PR agencies, but the best one for you will depend on your goals, industry, and existing capabilities: What channels are you focused on? Are you primarily concerned with SEO, social media, reputation management, or traditional coverage? Are you in a specialized industry (e.g., healthcare, legal, travel) that might require a PR agency with niche expertise? Are you looking to help your business scale through country-wide or international coverage? What budget do you have to work with? Once you have a clear idea of your needs, you can better filter the results of your search. Look for Agencies in the Channels You Want To Target Start with the channel where you most want to show up. If SEO is the priority, check who ranks on page one for “[your industry] digital PR agency.” If AI visibility matters, ask two or three chatbots which digital PR agencies they’d recommend, since chatbots favor cited, data-backed content, and GEO-focused agencies like Siege Media tend to surface here. If bylines in traditional media are the goal, search “[Brand Name] case study” for brands you admire and see which agencies claim the work. Ask for Referrals Ask for references from current or past clients, or from colleagues who’ve worked with an agency you’re considering. Direct feedback often surfaces details a case study leaves out. Bake Digital PR Into Your Strategy While there are many digital PR services and agencies to choose from, only you can determine the one that best fits your brand’s goals and objectives. And that work’s now earning AI mentions, citations, and recommendations right alongside traditional rankings. One client, Vena Solutions, saw a 2,300% increase in blog link traffic after partnering with our digital PR team. Looking to take advantage of digital PR efforts? Check out our digital PR services and get a free ROI assessment. Frequently Asked Questions There’s a lot that goes into making sure your content gets the coverage it needs. Here are some frequently asked questions about digital PR services. What Is Digital PR? Digital PR, short for digital public relations, is a marketing strategy focused on earning brand visibility and backlinks through online publications and journalist relationships, rather than traditional print or broadcast media. Businesses that invest in digital PR can secure coverage in online publications and through influencer partnerships, building both their digital footprint and their backlink profile. What Do Digital PR Agencies Do? Digital PR agencies help businesses and organizations improve their online presence, reputation, and relationships with their target audience through various digital channels. They execute campaigns and strategies to increase brand awareness, credibility, and visibility through: Media outreach Social media management Content creation Influencer marketing Online reputation management Why Is Digital PR Important? Digital PR is important because it helps businesses reach their target audience online while building relationships with the influencers and journalists who shape their industry’s coverage. It also improves online reputation and drives measurable increases in website traffic and leads. Most importantly, digital PR supports SEO by earning high-quality backlinks that improve search rankings and boost long-term visibility. Does Digital PR Help With AI Search Visibility? Yes, digital PR can help you appear in AI search. The same signals that build traditional search authority, backlinks and mentions on trusted publications, are also what AI Overviews and LLMs draw from when generating answers. Digital PR campaigns built around original data and research tend to get cited by other sites. That same coverage also increasingly shows up in AI-generated answers, making a strong digital PR strategy just as valuable for AI visibility as it is for traditional rankings. How Can I Measure the Success of a Digital PR Campaign? You can measure the success of a digital PR campaign by tracking metrics such as website traffic, social media engagement, backlinks, and media mentions. It is important to set specific goals and track progress over time to determine the effectiveness of the campaign.

text: Log In Submit a Press Release Log In Get Started Newswire Educational Resources Explore Our Expert Advice, How-Tos and Guides Digital PR Services: What They Include and What They Cost Digital PR services earn your company coverage, mentions and links on online news sites and publications, and back that up with search-optimized content, an online media room and coverage monitoring. What they cost depends on scope: how much content is written, how many pitches go out and how much reporting you need. What is digital PR? Digital PR is public relations aimed at online outcomes. The goal is the same as any PR program, which the Public Relations Society of America (PRSA) describes as building "mutually beneficial relationships between organizations and their publics" ( PRSA ). The difference is where the results show up: in online articles, search results, links back to your site and social shares. That's where digital PR and SEO overlap. Google says that "one of the factors used to determine quality is understanding if other prominent websites link or refer to the content" ( Google ). Earned coverage on a respected site can give you that kind of reference. Digital PR vs. traditional PR Main targets: Traditional PR: Print, TV and radio outlets. Digital PR: Online publications, trade sites, blogs, newsletters. Typical outcomes: Traditional PR: Articles, segments, interviews. Digital PR: Online articles, links, mentions, social shares. Owned assets: Traditional PR: Press kits, fact sheets. Digital PR: Search-optimized releases, blog posts, an online media room. Measurement: Traditional PR: Coverage counts and clippings. Digital PR: Coverage, links, referral clicks and search visibility. The two overlap. A single announcement can earn a print article and an online one, and both can be tracked. What digital PR services include Search-optimized press releases Writing press releases is the first duty the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics lists for PR specialists ( BLS ). Digital PR adds search optimization: a clear headline, the words your audience actually searches for and a useful page someone would want to read and share. One caution: Google lists "links with optimized anchor text in articles, guest posts, or press releases distributed on other sites" as an example of link spam ( Google spam policies ). The search value of digital PR comes from coverage journalists choose to write, not from stuffing links into releases. Blog content Blog posts give each announcement more context and give journalists and searchers something useful to land on. They also keep your site active between big announcements. An online media room An online media room, or newsroom, is the page on your site where journalists find your releases, company facts, images and media contacts. In Muck Rack's State of Journalism survey, 37% of journalists said high-resolution images were among the most valuable parts of a pitch, and 40% valued original data or research ( University of Minnesota summary ). A media room keeps those assets in one place. Media targeting and pitching Digital PR depends on reaching the right online journalists and editors. The same survey found that 62% of journalists prefer to be pitched in a one-to-one email, 69% prefer pitches under 200 words and 70% most value clear relevance to their beat. Good targeting comes before good pitching. Social amplification Sharing earned coverage and announcements on your own social channels extends their reach. If you also work with influencers, the Federal Trade Commission says endorsements must disclose any "material connection" to the brand, including payment or free products ( FTC ). Monitoring and reporting Monitoring tracks where your company is mentioned and which coverage includes links. Reporting turns that into something you can act on: what ran, where, what it linked to and what it drove to your site. Digital PR and SEO: what it can and can't do What it can do: Earn coverage on sites your audience trusts Earn editorial links and references that Google says are one factor in judging quality Drive referral clicks from coverage to your site Build owned content, such as releases, blogs and a media room, that can be found in search What it can't do: Guarantee rankings. Google's ranking systems look at "many factors and signals," and links are only one of them ( Google ). Buy links safely. Google treats "buying or selling links for ranking purposes" as link spam. Paid links need to be marked rel="sponsored" or rel="nofollow" ( Google ). Work instantly. Google notes that "it may take several days after publishing a page for Google to find and crawl it" ( Google ), and earned coverage depends on journalists' own schedules. Here's what that looks like when it works. The CE Shop earned 34 high-value SEO backlinks through earned media, which Liz Meitus, SVP of Corporate Communications, described as "...equivalent to the output we previously needed a full-time employee to achieve." The company also saw a 160% increase in PR-driven clicks. What digital PR services cost Providers package and price digital PR in different ways, so the useful question is what drives cost and what you get for it. What drives the price Content volume: How many releases, blog posts and media room updates are included Outreach volume: How many pitches go out each month, and to how many targeted outlets Tools: Whether media databases and monitoring are included Strategy: Whether planning and a press release calendar are part of the package Reporting: How detailed reports are and how often you get them The in-house benchmark If you're comparing an outside provider with hiring, start with salary data. The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics puts the median annual wage for public relations specialists at $74,750. The lowest 10% earned less than $44,110, and the highest 10% earned more than $135,150 ( BLS ). Those figures are wages only. They don't include benefits, tools such as media databases or any extra content support. Pricing questions to ask Is this a monthly program, a one-time project or something else? Exactly which deliverables are included each month? Are media database and monitoring costs included? What happens if a pitch doesn't earn coverage? Are any placements paid? If so, they're advertising and should be labeled. Red flags Guaranteed placements in named outlets for a fee, presented as earned coverage "Link packages" or paid links that pass ranking credit, which Google treats as link spam Reports that count activity, such as emails sent, but not results How to evaluate a digital PR provider Before you sign, ask to see: A sample plan or press release calendar Writing samples, including an optimized release and a blog post How the provider builds media lists for your industry A sample report showing coverage, links and referral traffic Results for clients like you, with named outlets where possible Where Newswire PRO fits Newswire PRO is a boutique PR team for companies that lack the resources, time or know-how to get media visibility. Its packages include several of the services described above: CONTENT PRO: press release calendar, 12 written press releases, SEO optimization, 1 blog a month, an online media room and reporting. Social posting (1 post per press release) is an optional add-on. MEDIA PRO: custom media targeting, media pitching (up to 10 pitches per month), media monitoring, media databases and reporting. TOTAL PRO: both together, an outsourced PR team at a fraction of the cost of a traditional agency. Turnaround is approximately 3–5 days. Pricing depends on the package, so contact us for pricing. PRO clients have earned 42+ media placements, including Forbes, PEOPLE and US News & World Report. See Newswire PRO's press release writing and media pitching services , or explore the full range of PR services . Frequently asked questions What is the difference between digital PR and SEO? SEO covers everything that helps your site appear in search, from content to technical setup. Digital PR is one input: it earns coverage and links from other sites, which Google says is one factor in judging quality. Do digital PR services guarantee backlinks? No provider can guarantee earned links, because journalists decide what to publish and whether to link. Paid links aren't a safe substitute; Google treats buying links for ranking purposes as link spam. How much do digital PR services cost? It depends on scope: content volume, pitch volume, tools and reporting. As a benchmark, the BLS reports a median annual wage of $74,750 for PR specialists, before benefits or tools. How long does digital PR take to show results? It varies. Coverage depends on journalists' schedules, and Google says it may take several days after a page is published for Google to find and crawl it. Is digital PR worth it for a small company? It can be, if you have news worth sharing and a way to produce and pitch it consistently. See PR services for small business for where to start.
